The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c417858c9fe566da), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 11. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix E and an initial discriminant h0. Consider families hx, x ∈ Fb 2, obtained from h0 by adjoining new prime factors with linear activation functions on Fb 2. No old factor is removed; the signed factor belonging to an odd prime q is q∗ = (−1/q)q. Suppose the local twisting classes at 2N are constant. For each family let k define an imaginary field satisfying the standing Heegner conditions, with (k, hx) = 1 for every x. Each new prime must either split in K or satisfy tq = 0. Assume that the following bounds are fixed independently of b: (i) a bound for ω(k); (ii) a bound for the length of the finite quotient of Sel2∞ (E(h0)/K) by its divisible subgroup; (iii) a constant B. Assume this base Selmer group has corank one. Suppose, for every x ̸= 0, the product L(E(hx), s)L(E(hxk), s) has a simple zero and 2j(P|hx|(hx)) − 4w(hx) − s(hx) − s(hxk) ≤ B. (3.9) Then, for sufficiently large b, the base product has a simple zero. The dimension threshold depends only on the fixed base and the displayed bounds, not on the number or sizes of the new primes. The field K may vary with the family.
